structured.answer: I'd open the account at Psagot and buy the IBI fund, "אי.בי.אי. מחקה (4A) ת"א 125". The page marks that pair "הזול" (the cheapest). After 10 years it shows about 86,045 ₪ left, but that's with the page's own numbers (10,000 ₪ now, 500 a month, 7% a year), not my 30,000.

stuck.where: Amount fields at the top (סכום היום 10,000, הפקדה חודשית 500)
stuck.why: The task said put money in every month but gave no amounts, so I left the page's numbers. That means 86,045 isn't really my number, since I have 30,000.

stuck.where: The fund list, the −0.04% next to my chosen fund
stuck.why: I saw a minus and at first thought the fund loses money every year. The others are worse (−0.37% to −0.54%), so I took this one as the least bad. I'm not sure what it means.

stuck.where: The top card says ₪ 1,390 פחות for the fund, but the fund list says −1,030 ₪
stuck.why: Two different numbers for the same comparison. I didn't get which one is right.

findings.what: The final amount is calculated on 10,000 + 500 by default. Someone who doesn't change it takes away a number that isn't theirs.
findings.where: Screen 1–2, amount fields and the 86,045 ₪ card

findings.what: Minus signs on all the funds look like a loss. It's scary and unclear.
Two different numbers for how much more the fund costs (1,390 vs 1,030).
The fund name (אי.בי.אי) appears small, in a box in the middle of grey text, and I almost missed what I'm actually buying.
Too many banks that look alike, with notes about other prices for young people and soldiers. Hard to tell if one of them is cheaper for me.
Words like נאמן and דמי משמרת without an explanation next to them.
